choices: Providing a bigger table of characters than ASCII
Separating which character this is (a code point) from how it is stored (an encoding)
Making every character exactly two bytes
Replacing bytes with characters as the unit of storage
explanation: The bigger table is real and secondary. ASCII merged identity and storage — 'A' was 65 was the byte 01000001 — and prising them apart is what dissolves most text confusion. Unicode certainly does not fix the width: code points run to U+10FFFF and UTF-8 uses one to four bytes.
